content: The document was developed under the strategic guidance of Dr. Poonam Khetrapal Singh, the Regional Director, along with Dr. Pem Namgyal, Director of Programme Management, and Dr. Suman Rijal, Director of Communicable Diseases Surveillance (CDS) at WHO SEARO. The entire process was overseen by Dr. Sunil Bahl, Coordinator of COVAX, Immunization, and Vaccine Development. Dr. Sudhir Khanal, from IVD/CDS WHO SEARO, led the coordination and development of the technical document in collaboration with Dr. Sudhir Joshi, also from IVD/CDS WHO SEARO. Dr. Lalit Kant, a WHO consultant, played a pivotal role in updating the technical content of the document. The document also benefited from the expert contributions of participants from the Regional Workshop held in Dhaka from June 13–16, 2022. This workshop reviewed progress toward measles-rubella elimination and other priority vaccine-preventable disease (VPD) surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and response in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Participants included National EPI Programme Managers, VPD Surveillance Officers from Member States, WHO country office staff, UNICEF representatives, and other external collaborators. WHO Headquarters staff, including Dr. Anindya Bose and Dr. Heidi Soeters, reviewed the draft surveillance standards document and provided technical inputs. Additional contributions were made by WHO SEARO staff, including Dr. Jayantha Liyanage, Dr. Sigrun Roesel, Dr. Emmanuel Njambe, Dr. Lucky Sangal, Dr. Pankaj Bhatnagar, Ms. Uttara Aggarwal, Mr. Sharifuzzaman, Dr. Rajendra Bohara, Dr. Ariful Islam, Dr. Tanbir Islam, Dr. Subramanya Balakuntla Pattabhiramaiah, Dr. Ratnesh Murugan, Dr. Stephen Chacko, Dr. Paba Palihawadana, Dr. Aishath Thimna Latheef, Dr. Balwinder Chawla, Dr. Khaing Khaing Gyi, Dr. Vinod Bura, Dr. Rahul Pradhan, Dr. Pasang Rai, Dr. Preshila Samarawera, Ms. Aree Moungsookjareoun, and Dr. Sudath Peiris. UNICEF’s Christopher Gregory provided inputs and coordinated contributions from the UNICEF team for various sections of the document. From the US CDC, Dr. Ahmed Kassem and Dr. Michelle Morales contributed to the document and coordinated inputs from various teams within the CDC.
